title: Causal Risk Ratio Estimation in Case-Control Data under Rare Prevalence and Unknown Densities
banked_reason: Typed D0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: incremental < field; paper_score_ceiling 6.3 < 7.4; no bounded same-topic salvage. Math and cited sources pass; independent validity gate confirms sound but over-framed scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered results establish known-smoothness uniform achievability and a balanced-null honest-length obstruction, rather than a complete statistical frontier for the causal risk ratio.
The separate control and case mixtures do not establish the mixed-smoothness point-risk lower bound, and the registry calibration has no matching sparse-registry converse.

The conservative derivative-envelope and Markov calibration has no delivered interval-length computation demonstrating practical usefulness, limiting the projected paper score alongside the unresolved optimality questions.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed the exact causal prevalence decomposition, full-positive-smoothness cubic-rate upper bounds, finite honest calibration, and a balanced-null causal adaptation obstruction. Math and source reviews passed, but matching mixed-smoothness point-risk and sparse-registry converses and evidence of informative interval width were not delivered, leaving the assessed tier incremental below the field floor. No Lean formalization was attempted; two editorial duplicate nodes remain disclosed in the archived graph.
tldr: For the exact causal risk ratio with unknown case and control densities, the leading doubly robust error is unsuppressed and the smooth correction error is multiplied by prevalence. Audited fixed-stratum cubic modules give a uniform rarity, smoothness and registry frontier on the unchanged positive Hölder class. Writing \(s_*=\min(s_g,s_h)\), its retrospective upper guarantee is root-\(n\) when \(s_h+s_*\ge d/2\) and either \(s_*\ge d/4\) or prevalence falls below the explicit correction threshold. Point-risk registry uncertainty is separate from the honest-length \(1/m\) term. At a balanced smooth null, honest intervals retain a control penalty independent of prevalence and a prevalence-weighted case penalty for every registry size. These lower bounds transfer to Sui et al.'s broader base risk-identification class; the estimator upper bounds remain on the regular subclass. The contribution is an exact causal specialization and audit of established methods, without a full minimax, adaptive-estimation, efficiency or computational-optimality claim.
gap: Prevalence-assisted causal identification, flexible weighted estimation, exact attribution corrections, higher-order functional methods and generic adaptation theory are established. The inspected sources do not give the joint RR-specific uniform positive-Hölder coverage audit and balanced-null honest-length conclusion.
fill: Exact algebra, computable conservative risk envelopes, binomial-calibrated coverage and causal common-target alternatives connect established ingredients. The claim is an incremental causal inference result, not a new general minimax mechanism.
